source_integrity.summary: Matching Git blob SHA for pending v2 and both staged Markdown sources; same reviewed revision.

schema_and_taxonomy.summary: Controlled Global Macro daily classification; required localized fields; strategic-competition phenomenon is registered.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: 14 Nov Saturday edition uses completed 13 Nov securities markets, published Oct PPI and oil/stock data, Q3 GDP and Sep retail periods without treating forecasts as observations.

factual_methodology.summary: BLS October PPI 0.3% m/m and 6.5% y/y; Treasury 10Y 4.98/5.10/5.15 dated; IEA Oct supply 105.4m b/d and inventory +52m bbl; Eurostat EU/EA GDP and ONS UK Q3; NBS China industrial/household price divergence verified against dated originals.

evidence_traceability.summary: 13 aligned source URLs across both locales, including BLS, Treasury, IEA, Eurostat, ONS, NBS and BCB. Sampled factual claims against directly retrievable originals and dated market press; no complete independent global corporate spread or flow panel.

research_depth.summary: EN 2909 / PT-BR 3176 substantive words; ten numbered analytic chapters, 2 quantitative charts, dated evidence table, causal flow, geographic comparison and counterfactual scenario tests; new IEA/BLS observations after prior cutoff.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two charts preserve identical numeric sequences across locales; US October PPI indices share unit/horizon with non-additivity warning; Treasury 10-year dated yield series has same instrument/horizon; flow and map describe qualified mechanisms.

bilingual_equivalence.summary: Both locales have same sourced numeric claims, reference URLs, chart series, scenario rows and region/causal mechanisms, idiomatic language and no conversational metadescriptions.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Prose concerns economics, financial channels and evidence, without product/pipeline self-reference; source references are at the end; 6+ analytically connected sections.

contrary_evidence.summary: Explicit crude versus diesel and freight divergence, monthly versus annual PPI, bond yields versus actual credit spreads, Brazil fiscal implementation versus Senate vote, UK/EA growth heterogeneity.

counterfactual_review.summary: Conditionally falsifiable oil, US restrictive-rate, European employment and Brazilian fiscal-risk scenarios; data needed to discriminate specified.

pipeline_validation.summary: Applied matching source depth and research visual syntax gates by direct connector read; full npm build and deployment not run during editorial review, reserved for publisher/CI.

contrary_evidence: Higher observed crude supply does not establish cheaper delivered diesel, but it reduces crude scarcity pressures.
Lower US monthly PPI does not imply lower annual inflation, and the next Fed decision is not predetermined.
Higher Treasury yields do not demonstrate cancelled AI investment or uniformly higher private loan rates.
Brazilian monthly retail increase does not reverse weak quarterly comparison.
limitations: No independent high-frequency survey of global corporate credit spreads or exact portfolio fund flows.
IEA forecast supply surplus is prospective; Gulf shipping risk and diesel/product availability remain uncertain.
British and euro-area Q3 GDP estimates are preliminary.
Brazilian fiscal package still faces additional legislative steps.
QA was an assistant evidence review using direct sources and deterministic in-chat checks, not an independent human peer review.
Full npm production build and live HTTP publication not yet verified.
notes: Approved reviewed staged revision 1 after source-vintage and parity audits, with explicit empirical limitations. Publisher must recheck all 3 Git blob hashes before generating public files.
